card.title: FLOTILLA
card.text: A flotilla is a small group of naval vessels operating together.
card.flavorText: Flotillas are compact naval formations composed of smaller vessels such as torpedo boats, submarines, and patrol craft. During WWII, all major navies organized flotillas to perform missions in coastal zones, rivers, and confined seas where larger ships could not operate effectively. The Kriegsmarine fielded both Schnellboot (e. fast boat) and U-boat flotillas. Schnellboote, named E-boats by the Allies, launched night raids in the Channel and North Sea, while U-boat flotillas, operating from Atlantic ports, waged an extended campaign against Allied shipping. The Royal Navy countered with motor torpedo boat flotillas and escort groups defending convoy routes and attacking Axis coastal traffic. The US Navy deployed PT boat flotillas in the Pacific, where they disrupted Japanese barge traffic, scouted invasion beaches, and ambushed supply convoys in island chains like the Solomons and Philippines. On inland waters, US river flotillas supported amphibious operations in Burma and China with shallow-draft gunboats and landing craft. Soviet flotillas along the Volga and Danube supported ground offensives, while Italian MAS boats and Japanese fast attack units challenged Allied control of narrow seas. Despite their small size, flotillas played decisive roles in local battles, often shaping broader strategic outcomes.
